title: Mullins From the Logo Stuns Duke
dek: Down 19 in the first half to top overall seed Duke, UConn won 73-72 on freshman Braylon Mullins's 35-foot 3-pointer with 0.4 seconds left.

setup.text: The regional final fell on the 27th anniversary of UConn's 77-74 upset of Duke for its first national title. The programs had met in the tournament four times since 1990, Duke winning in 1990 and 1991 and UConn in 1999 and the 2004 Final Four. The 1990 game was decided by Christian Laettner's buzzer-beater in this same round.

Duke (35-2) was the No. 1 overall seed and No. 1 in the AP poll after winning the ACC regular-season and tournament titles. Its star was All-American freshman Cameron Boozer, averaging 22.4 points and 10.3 rebounds, playing alongside his twin brother, Cayden.

UConn (32-5), seeded second and ranked seventh, was chasing a third national title in four seasons, something no program had done since UCLA in the 1970s. After a 72-52 loss to St. John's in the Big East final, the Huskies beat Furman, UCLA and Michigan State; Tarris Reed Jr. opened the tournament with 31 points and 27 rebounds.

Freshman Braylon Mullins of Greenfield, Ind., a McDonald's All-American and Indiana's 2025 Mr. Basketball, had once listed Duke among his top 10 schools before canceling a planned visit to Durham and choosing UConn. He was averaging 12.0 points but, by ESPN's account, had been mired in a late-season shooting slump.

game.text: Reed's two free throws 21 seconds in gave UConn a 2-0 lead. It would be the Huskies' last lead until the final 0.4 seconds. Duke answered with seven straight points and went up 22-12 on a Cayden Boozer 3 with 13:24 left in the half.

UConn started Alex Karaban on Cameron Boozer, and Boozer finished over and around him or found open teammates when help came. A 14-0 Duke run, the largest against UConn since it rejoined the Big East in 2020-21, according to ESPN Research, made it 40-21, and Duke led 44-25 late in the half.

UConn made one of its 11 first-half 3-point attempts and trailed 44-29 at the break, when the Boozer twins had 27 points between them to UConn's 29. With 1:33 left in the half, UConn's win probability had dipped to 1.3 percent.

Duke stretched it to 50-33 on Patrick Ngongba II's alley-oop early in the second half. Reed, who scored 11 points in the first nine minutes after halftime, kept answering: his steal and dunk cut it to 10, and his dunk with 11:15 left made it 56-49 and drew a Duke timeout. With seven minutes left, UConn still had not made a 3 in the half.

sequence.text: Silas Demary Jr. hits a corner 3 off a Reed pass, UConn's first make from deep in the half after seven misses and only its second of the game.
Nikolas Khamenia answers with a 3 for Duke, from Cameron Boozer. The lead is back to 10.
Demary hits again, from the opposite corner on a Solo Ball feed. UConn calls timeout.
Ball drives for a layup, draws a foul on Cameron Boozer and makes the free throw, capping a 10-2 UConn run.
Cameron Boozer pulls up from eight feet to push the lead back to four.
After more than a minute and a half without a point by either team, Ngongba makes one of two free throws. Duke leads by five.
Ball's free throw at 1:31 has made it a four-point game. Now Reed steals a Cameron Boozer pass.
Karaban, 0-for-5 from 3 to that point, buries a 26-footer. Duke's lead is one.
Cameron Boozer muscles inside for a 9-foot pull-up with 28.9 seconds left. UConn calls timeout.
Demary is fouled by Cameron Boozer with 10 seconds left. He misses the first free throw and makes the second.

UConn presses. The inbound goes to Cameron Boozer, out to Dame Sarr, then to Cayden Boozer near midcourt. Rather than hold the ball and take a foul, Cayden tries a long pass over the trap toward two open teammates. Demary gets a hand on it, and Mullins scoops it up.

Mullins pushes the ball ahead to Karaban, who sees Cameron Boozer on him and gives it right back. In rhythm, at the edge of the midcourt March Madness logo, Mullins lets go from 35 feet: nothing but net. The clock shows 0.3, officials set it at 0.4, and Karaban swats away Duke's long inbound pass.

quotes.text: It just felt like the window where you've just got to let March Madness take over.
quotes.role: UConn head coach, on not calling a timeout

quotes.text: I knew I had to put one up. Man, I'm just happy that was the one that went down tonight.
The Indiana kid sent us to Indianapolis.
I don't have the words. I don't have the words.

aftermath.text: Reed, with 26 points, nine rebounds and four blocks, was named the East Regional's Most Outstanding Player.

Six days later at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, UConn beat Illinois 71-62 in the Final Four. Reed had 17 points and 11 rebounds, and Mullins scored 15, including a 3 with 52 seconds left that made it 66-59.

On April 6, Michigan beat UConn 69-63 for its first national title since 1989, becoming the first team to beat UConn in the Sweet 16 or later since the 2009 Final Four. UConn shot a season-low 30.9 percent; Karaban had 17 points and 11 rebounds in his final college game.
UConn finished 34-6. It was the program's first loss in seven national championship games.
On April 18, Mullins announced that he would pass on the NBA draft and return for his sophomore season.

legacy.text: AP's Noah Trister placed the shot alongside Christian Laettner's for Duke in the 1992 regional final and Kris Jenkins' 2016 title-winner for Villanova.

By AP's count from a Sports Reference list, only 16 times before had a team trailing in the Sweet 16 or later won on a last-second shot. Two were UConn's: Tate George in 1990 and Richard Hamilton in 1998.
It was Duke's third straight season ended in stunning fashion, after an Elite Eight loss to No. 11 seed NC State in 2024 and a blown lead against Houston in the 2025 Final Four.
Khamenia, whose 3 had put Duke up 10 with 6:37 left, later committed to UConn as a transfer.

conflicts.source_says: 0.4 seconds left (AP, ESPN, UConn recap; Duke: 'less than one second'). Live calls said 0.3 (CBS's Ian Eagle, Duke radio, Westwood One); the CBS crew then noted a tenth of a second had been added. Sequence uses 0:00.4.
AP, ESPN and CBS Sports: 35 feet. UConn's recap: 'a 40-foot heave' and 'from nearly 40 feet.' UConn radio (Mike Crispino, per Awful Announcing): 'a 45-footer.' Narrative uses 35 feet.

unsure: Nickname: AP headlines called it 'Mullins Madness!' (game story) and 'Mullins' Miracle' (analysis piece), and the site's 2026 season story uses 'The Mullins Miracle.' Neither is confirmed as an established nickname, so nickname is null.
Why the tenth of a second was added (presumably a replay review) is not stated in any print source found; the narrative says only that the clock went from 0.3 to 0.4.
The CBS broadcast audio suggests Caleb Foster threw Duke's final inbound (the play-by-play shows Foster entering at 0:00), but no print source names him, so he is not named.
AP's account says Mullins picked the ball up 'near midcourt'; ESPN says 'in the backcourt.' The narrative avoids the distinction.
